definition: Precocious means advanced or developing far ahead of one's age.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word precocious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know precocious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By seven she had a precocious ear for languages, ordering the family's dinner in passable Portuguese after a week abroad.
A quick student picks things up fast for any age; precocious means performing years beyond your age.
Prodigy-level goes past precocious — not just ahead of other children, but astonishing even among grown masters.

Early-blooming borrows the garden's calendar: a talent or a person arriving at full flower ahead of the usual season. It is gentle praise and stays close to the plant picture. Precocious makes the same point as a sharper judgment about age — performance measurably years ahead of it.

Forward once meant what precocious means — a child ahead of their years — but to a modern ear it has soured into boldness: a forward child interrupts adults and pushes into conversations. Precocious keeps the ahead-of-age praise without any hint of cheek.

The science-fair judges assumed the seismograph was a kit until its eleven-year-old builder showed the judges the spring she had wound herself, the pendulum she had re-tuned after the first quake read low, and the fix she had borrowed from a 1930s engineering paper.
Precocious was the word every judge wrote, because the work was not good for eleven — it was good, and eleven.
Precocious is the exact word because it names development advanced far ahead of one's age — the calendar says child, the performance says otherwise.
The Latin root means 'ripened early,' and the word keeps that image: fruit sweet ahead of the harvest.
It praises timing as much as talent, and it belongs to the young; past a certain age, early ripening is just ripeness.

Its mirror in this unit is embryonic: an embryonic talent is barely formed, a precocious one has arrived early.
For skill without any claim about age, gifted does the plainer work.

Okafor,' which made the family laugh: Dele was eight.
He had entered the open division by mail, and his qualifying score placed him in the top twenty of a field made up almost entirely of high schoolers.
The league's director drove out to verify that the handwriting, and the boy, were real.
